institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I have thought about potentially working as a medical doctor in Norway in the future, so coming there on exchange was an incredible opportunity to get a feeling of how life could be there.
Language - I can speak the foreign language of the patients and doctors, which makes communication a lot more convenient.
Nature/experiences outside of my clinical practice - a place that has a lot of potential.
Good academic experience and relationships + exploring a new culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I was in contact with my administrative superviser from UiT, who helped with practical information regarding my clinical exchange programme.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: As mentioned above + I got a little tour of the hospital so I knew where to go my first day.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I received information about housing from UiT, where it was easy to apply for housing through Samskipnaden. Though it would have been helpful if I had known the confirmed exact dates for my exchange sooner, hence I only received that information just in time for the housing deadline.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There are no housing on campus. It is easy and convenient to get around on foot or take the bus - fairly inexpensive as a student with a monthly pass.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I liked that I lived in a student dorm with shared kitchen - that way I got to know other exchange students and Norwegians living on my floor.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I am on a practical exchange, so I did not sign up for any specific courses

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: When needed, I asked my supervisor from UCPH for advise in the registration process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful - I got the clinical departments I wished for exempt the surgical one (1/3).

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not applicable for me.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was a clinical exchange, and I suppose the level was similar to Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
It was less structured at UiT compared to UCPH, since I was the only one on exchange at the department at the time. I would have wished for more responsibility and engagement from some of the doctors regarding my clinical practices and learning outcomes - often times I was left alone and had to find a task to do/a doctor to follow. That was mentally hard over a long period, when you don't feel as welcome or taken care of in a new place. This was primarily relevant for my 5 weeks time at the surgical department.
Contrastly, I felt very welcomed and taken care of in the Anesthesia department, where I because of that also learned immensely!

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
5 weeks clinical practice in Hematology at UNN
5 weeks clinical practice in Cardiothoracic surgery at UNN
2 weeks clinical practice in Anesthesiology at UNN

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Clinical practice in Hematology and Anesthesiology at UNN - doctors in both departments were super friendly and welcoming towards me, where they made me feel a part of their department and integrated me in their clinical work --> I learned a lot and had a good time:)

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The housing I rented was unfurnished regardless of a bed, table and chair. So I had to spend a lot of money and time in the beginning of my exchange to purchase basic household stuff and inventory.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food/groceries was a lot more expensive than in Denmark - especially fruit and vegetables, and even more so if you wanted to buy organic, as I normally do.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
On own initiative, I joined the TSI volleyball club and had practice with them - it was a lot of fun and good socially too.
I also joined the knitting club for exchange students - very cozy and nice.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
I participated in:
TSI; student physical activity clubs.
Knitting club for exchange students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The knitting club, if you like to knit/want to learn it - a fun way to meet others and hangout.
TSI: if you like to play a specific sport, it is fun to join and meet likeminded people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go on a lot of hikes/skiing in the surrounding mountains of Tromsø - it is even possible to go to many incredible places with the bus. There are DNT huts where you can stay overnight too.
You can rent outdoor equipment for free from Turbo in the city center - as long as you have a Norwegian Phone number and address in Tromsø.
Go dog sledding in the winter season. Whale watching/boat tour on the Fjords. Take a trip to other parts of Norway; Lofoten.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I felt at home very easily, since the Norwegian culture and people are quite similar to Danish.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a sport in TSI, where the locals also participate.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not applicable.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed that I could talk Danish, with some Norwegian words, to the Norwegians, and them speaking in Norwegian to me - that made it easy for me to converse with the local people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Apply for housing in Tromsø through Samskipnaden - I can highly recommend staying at Dramsvegen Panorama in a room with private bathroom but shared kitchen - very good social life and ideal location; close to both UiT/UNN and the city center. Very convenient with the bus too.
Remember to enjoy the fjords surrounding Tromsø - whether it is for skiing/hiking/snow shoes - incredible views and a lot of fun. Easy to access even when taking the bus.
Prioritise participating in the introductory week at the beginning of the semester (start January or mid August) - an easy way to get to know other exchange students and get a good social life - I unfortunately missed out on this, since my exchange first began start March.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Trust the process - even though you get the final dates/confirmation of your exchange at the receiving institution rather late - you can be sure that you are going and that you have a spot.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Feeling at home in Tromsø and being able to speak Danish/Norwegian with the locals without a lot of misunderstanding.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
The language was difficult to understand specifically the first 1-2 weeks in the hospital, but afterwards I understood mostly and had minor issues with conversations.
Socially, it was a bit challenging to become a part of a friend groups, since I arrived in March, and all the other exchange students had started in January, and there were no given social acitivities through my studies etc.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
